metadata.case_name: FUNG KWOK KI v. WING SANG CONSTRUCTION CO LTD AND OTHERS

plaintiff.occupation_before: Lift Technician II employed by Ryoden Elevator Co. Ltd.

injuries.description: permanent residual brain damage in the form of impaired higher mental functions including dysarthria, dysphagia and mild upper limb dysfunction
source: After a prolonged period of surgical and medical treatment, the plaintiff has made a partial recovery and is left with permanent residual brain damage in the form of impaired higher mental functions including dysarthria, dysphagia and mild upper limb dysfunction.
injuries.icd_description: Diffuse injury of multiple parts of brain

injuries.description: Contusion injuries to his head, neck and front chest wall
injuries.body_part: head, neck and front chest wall
source: He suffered contusion injuries to his head, neck and front chest wall.

injuries.description: Thoracic spinal injury with paralysis; spinal cord damage at T7 level (complete spinal cord injury)
source: The clinical diagnosis was head injury, thoracic spinal injury with paralysis and fracture of left femur.
His neurogenic urinary and bowel disturbance are caused by the spinal cord damage at T7 level, and like his paraplegia, will be permanent.
Physical examination showed tetraplegia with signs of complete spinal cord injury.
injuries.icd_description: Complete lesion of thoracic spinal cord

source: The clinical diagnosis was head injury, thoracic spinal injury with paralysis and fracture of left femur.
He had internal fixation of his spine and left femur.

manifestations.description: unconscious on admission; deep coma with Glasgow Coma Score of 3/15
vegetative state then improved to Glasgow Coma Score of 12-13/15
tetraplegia with signs of complete spinal cord injury
double incontinence (neurogenic urinary and bowel disturbance)
neuropathic bladder with poor or uncoordinated detrusor contraction and without any sensation of filling or distension; managed by Clean Intermittent Catheterisation five times daily
severe pressure (back) sores requiring multiple debridement and Gluteal maximus myocutaneous flap (surgical wound later broke down)

treatments_received.treatment: Admission to Accident and Emergency Department; resuscitation; intubation; intravenous infusion; neck collar and spine board
source: He was admitted into the Accident and Emergency Department of Kwong Wah Hospital immediately after the accident on 5 July 2000. ... Resuscitation was carried out. He was given intubation, intravenous infusion, neck collar and spine board.

treatments_received.treatment: Admission to Intensive Care Unit under orthopaedic department
source: He was admitted to Intensive Care Unit under orthopaedic department for further management.

treatments_received.treatment: Internal fixation of spine and left femur
source: He stayed in ICU until 24 July and had internal fixation of his spine and left femur.
He had internal fixation of his spine and left femur.

treatments_received.treatment: Multiple debridement of pressure sores; frequent dressings and debridements
source: He developed severe back sore problem. He received multiple debridement to his sores without much improvement.
However, the surgical wound broke down later and he was treated with frequent dressings and debridements with gradual improvement.
treatments_received.vmis_procedure: Local excision or destruction of lesion or tissue of skin and subcutaneous tissue

source: Orthopaedic surgeons performed Gluteal maximus myocutaneous flap on him on 25 October 2000.

treatments_received.treatment: Percutaneous release for triggering contracted left middle finger (3 September 2001)
source: In August 2001, he was transferred back to Kwong Wah Hospital Orthopaedic Department for his triggering contracted left middle finger. Percutaneous release was done on 3 September 2001.

treatments_received.treatment: Transfer to Wong Tai Sin Hospital for further rehabilitation (13 July 2001)
source: As his condition was stable, he was transferred to Wong Tai Sin Hospital for further rehabilitation on 13 July 2001.

treatments_received.treatment: Rehabilitation and speech therapy; speech therapy sessions
source: He was transferred ... for further rehabilitation and speech therapy before being finally discharged home on 26 April 2002.
Cost of Speech Therapy ...

treatments_received.treatment: Clean Intermittent Catheterisation five times daily
source: He is being managed by Clean Intermittent Catheterisation five times daily.

treatments_received.treatment: Use of laxatives and suppositories for bowel management
source: His bowel problem needs to have continued management with laxative and suppositories.

losses.description: Loss of society of the plaintiff by his wife (statutory amount allowed)
Full loss of earnings; plaintiff will never be able to work again
Now permanently wheelchair-bound and requires full time care

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life

losses.description: Permanent inability to use lower limbs; permanently wheelchair-bound
